transcript.content: Hi, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I feel like dispatch and compliance have been tracking what I’m doing at work—like my route changes in the computer system, and then little comments come over the radio that feel connected to it. People say it’s just normal oversight, but I can tell some of the other drivers are reporting on me.
Have you been feeling unusually high, euphoric, or excessively energetic lately?
No, not really. I wouldn’t say I’ve felt high or euphoric. My energy’s been pretty normal, I think.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is actually there?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed hearing voices when nobody’s there.
How long have you been feeling that dispatch, compliance, or other drivers are tracking or reporting on you?

It’s been about two months that it’s felt really clear to me. Like, before that maybe I wondered a little, but the computer stuff and the radio comments have seemed connected for around the past two months.
Have you noticed yourself becoming much less interested in seeing people or doing things you usually care about?

Yeah… I have. I used to like singing with the choir and having the softball team over, but lately I just don’t feel like doing any of it. Most days after my shift, I end up sitting at the kitchen table with my planner open, and I just can’t get myself to start dinner, make calls, or really do anything.
Have there been any times when these beliefs about being tracked were happening even though you were not feeling down or uninterested in things?

Yes. It’s not only when I’m feeling down or not interested in things. Even on days when I’m just trying to work normally, I still notice it—the route changes in the computer, the radio comments, and certain drivers acting like they’re reporting on me. People say it’s just regular oversight, but it doesn’t feel that way to me.
Aside from the radio at work, have you heard a voice speaking to you when no one was actually there?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, aside from the radio stuff at work, I haven’t heard a voice talking to me when nobody was there.
Have people told you that your speech has been hard to follow or that your thoughts seem jumbled?
Not that I know of. I mean, I don’t think people have said my speech is hard to follow. Sometimes I get distracted or lose my place, but I haven’t been told my thoughts sound jumbled.
Have you felt as if someone or something was controlling your thoughts or actions?

Not exactly controlling my thoughts or moving my body, no. It’s more like they’re watching and tracking what I’m doing — dispatch and compliance through the computer, the route changes, and the little comments on the radio. And some drivers, I can tell they’re reporting on me.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being broadcast so that other people could know them?

Not like my thoughts are being broadcast, no. It’s more that I think dispatch and compliance can track what I’m doing through the computer system, like my route changes, and then I hear little comments on the radio. Even if people say it’s normal oversight, I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me.
Since these experiences started, have they been present continuously for at least one month?
Yes. It’s been going on pretty steadily for about two months now — the tracking through the computer system and the radio comments. It’s felt clear to me that whole time.
Since this started, have you had a period when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve had a time where I needed way less sleep and still felt energized. My sleep has been off some, but not like that.
Since this started, have you found yourself speaking much less than usual?

I don’t think I’m talking less exactly. It’s more like I just don’t feel like doing much. I used to sing with choir and have the softball team over, and now I don’t really want to. Most days after my shift I just sit at the kitchen table with my planner open, and I can’t get myself to start dinner or make calls or anything.
From the very first time you started wondering that people at work might be tracking or reporting on you, has it been six months or more?
No, not six months. It’s been more like about two months since the tracking and the radio comments started feeling clear to me.
During this time, have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?
I’m not sure I’d call it depressed most of the day nearly every day. I’ve felt pretty down and worn out at times, but I haven’t really been tracking it like that.
Have you been feeling sad or empty nearly every day?
I don’t really know. I’ve had sad moments, yeah, but I wouldn’t say I feel sad or empty nearly every day. It’s more like I feel tired and kind of stuck.
Have you lost your appetite?
I haven’t really noticed losing my appetite. I mean, some days I don’t feel like eating much, but I can’t say it’s been a clear change.
Have you been unable to enjoy things you usually like doing nearly every day?

Yeah… I guess so. I don’t really feel like doing things I used to like, like singing with the choir or having the softball team over. Most days after my shift I just end up sitting at the kitchen table with my planner open, but I can’t make myself start dinner or make calls or do anything.
For at least two weeks during this period, did you feel depressed most of the day nearly every day?
I’m not sure I’d call it depressed most of the day nearly every day. I’ve had low times, but I don’t think it was like that for two straight weeks.
During this time, was there ever a period of at least two weeks when the tracking and radio comments were happening but you were not feeling down or uninterested in things?

Yes. There were times for more than a couple weeks where I wasn’t really feeling down like that, but the tracking was still going on. Dispatch and compliance were still watching my route changes in the system, and I’d hear little comments over the radio. Even if people said it was just normal oversight, I could tell some drivers were reporting on me.
